title: November/December 2026
gist: Table of contents for Foreign Affairs' November/December 2026 issue, listing essays on U.S. military power, war technology, chokepoints, economic espionage, AI empires and bust, the Iran war, China's decline and dollar dominance.

insights.claim: Foreign Affairs' November/December 2026 issue leads with William McRaven on the limits of American power and the delusion of force, and Mara Karlin on why the future of war cannot escape the past.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Signals elite-policy framing of U.S. military overreach.

insights.claim: Two pieces on Iran, by Ali Vaez and Mohammad Ayatollahi Tabaar, frame the war as a 'new forever war' in which America and Iran fight on without victory and Tehran escalates to drive America out of the Middle East.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: The Iran conflict is treated as protracted, a persistent energy and risk factor.

insights.claim: Henry Farrell, Abraham Newman and Yeling Tan argue in 'The Chokepoint Trap' that the search for economic security will end in geopolitical calamity, while David Cohen argues America should spy on foreign companies to help its own.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Economic-security policy (export controls, espionage) is a major theme for supply-chain risk.

insights.claim: The issue pairs Ferguson, Klaassen and Schmidt on 'Empires of AI' with Ruchir Sharma on 'The Global AI Bust' and Imas, El-Erian and Manyika on AI as a choice with a narrow but feasible path to collective good.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Signals both imperial and bust framings of AI; Sharma's piece asks what survives when the boom ends.

insights.claim: Carl Minzner covers China's long twilight of demographic decline and political paralysis, and Zongyuan Zoe Liu covers Beijing's green path to ending dollar dominance.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: China's demographic and currency strategies are headline topics of the issue.

insights.claim: The reviews section includes Pratap Bhanu Mehta on liberalism, Beverly Gage on John Foster Dulles, a nuclear-deterrence exchange involving Gottemoeller, and Lardy and Froman on 'Who Killed the Global Economy?'
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Lardy and Froman debate the real roots of the next crisis.
